source_title: Book: Kanye West showed up unannounced, stayed 4 days at $295m Malibu mansion
source_excerpt: A $295 million Malibu mansion designed by Pritzker Prize-winning Japanese architect Tadao Ando was quietly on the market when rapper Kanye West arrived unannounced and stayed for four days, according to a new biography of his former wife, Kim Kardashian. An October 2026 report by the New York Post drew on journalist Jonathan Van Meterâs book 'Citizen Kim' to recount how West persuaded the estateâs owners to let him inside, set up an office beside the pool and hold meetings there. The episode offers a glimpse into the rapperâs fascination with Andoâs architecture, even as Westâs own Ando-designed Malibu property remains mired in restoration and foreclosure complications.Kanye Westâs unexpected visit to the $295 million estateArt collectors Maria and Bill Bell commissioned the mansion in Malibuâs exclusive Paradise Cove area. Known as the âBig Andoâ, the approximately 42,000-square-foot property took 15 years to build and features the Japanese architectâs signature use of concrete, geometric forms and carefully framed ocean views. According to 'Citizen Kim', West drove to the estate without scheduling an appointment through celebrity real estate agent Kurt Rappaport, who represented the owners. Instead, he reportedly arrived at the gate and introduced himself.When the owner hesitated to let him in, West allegedly invoked Elvis Presley to make his case. âIf Elvis Presley came to your door and rang your buzzer, would you let him in? This is that,â he reportedly said. The visit went far beyond a conventional property viewing. Van Meter writes that West remained at the estate for four days, setting up an office by the pool and holding meetings because he wanted to experience what it felt like to work inside an Ando-designed home.The mansion had reportedly been marketed privately for $295 million. In September 2021, he purchased a separate oceanfront house on Malibu Road for $57.25 million. The roughly 4,000-square-foot residence had originally been commissioned by financier and art collector Richard Sachs and was completed in 2013 after a seven-year design and construction process. It was also designed by Ando, whose limited portfolio of standalone residential buildings in the United States makes the properties particularly notable among architecture enthusiasts.According to the New York Post, Andoâs executive architect for the Malibu Road project, Ron Radziner, used the informal name âLittle Andoâ for Westâs house, distinguishing it from the much larger Paradise Cove estate. But the renovation took a destructive turn, leaving the home without many of the features required for ordinary habitation.From architectural landmark to an unfinished concrete shellAfter purchasing the Malibu Road house, West hired contractor Tony Saxon to carry out the renovation. The changes stripped the residence of much of its original design and left an unfinished concrete structure exposed to the coastal environment. The alterations also triggered a legal dispute. Saxon sued West for $1.7 million over the renovation project. According to the New York Post, a Los Angeles jury awarded Saxon $140,000 in March 2026 for lost wages and medical expenses. West eventually abandoned the project and listed the property in December 2023 for $53 million.
